_superseded: An independent review of prep/d-series-topk-tail@bd70a165 reopened this adoption. The single lower-bound violation I had recorded as a 'bounded open numerical observation' was a real defect: the tail was reconstructed as `1 - sum(support)`, which crosses float32 resolution once the support holds nearly all the mass -- our own measured support mass reached 1.000001 -- and the code then DROPPED the tail term whenever either mass rounded to zero, when only a zero REFERENCE mass may make a forward-KL term vanish. The findings below were computed under that arithmetic and are NOT the adopted evidence. They are kept because a1/a2/a3 are real paid measurements and because the superseded numbers are what the repair has to be judged against.
_verdict_is_across_subruns: NO SINGLE SUBRUN answered everything. a1 produced A/B/C and the DEPTH half of E; a2 independently CONFIRMED C with the corrected in-run analysis but lost stage D to a bare policy id and its record arrived truncated; a3 measured D. Every answer below names the subrun that produced it.

A_reference_top200_mass._reading: the median position is essentially fully covered and the TAIL is the finding: at the 1st percentile the Top-200 holds 86% of the mass, and somewhere in the mixture a position holds 2.3%. A mean of 0.994 hides both, which is why the distribution was asked for.

B_full_vs_k_plus_1._the_one_violation: one of 17,420 per-item scores had the K+1 KL exceed the full one by 2.968e-04 absolute / 2.2e-03 relative. A coarsening cannot do that. It is NOT reproducible: synthetic float32, float64 and bf16 checks across six distribution shapes show zero violations. It affects no per-candidate score and no decision. Recorded as a bounded open numerical observation -- not claimed as float noise, which is unproven, nor as a defect, which the evidence does not support.

C_depth_decisions._how_it_is_trustworthy: the in-run analysis was WRONG and said so: it aggregated candidates by a pooled mean where the operator uses domain_balanced_score, and its own reconstruction check flagged rounds 4 and 5 as disagreeing with the operator. Corrected by importing the operator's aggregation and re-analysing OFFLINE from the recorded per-item scores -- no GPU time repaid. The reconstruction now matches the operator in every round, and the driver RAISES if it ever does not.
C_depth_decisions._reading: ZERO of 8 rounds move. The Top-200 protocol would choose the same layer every round, so the removal orders are identical and nothing in the comparison is counterfactual.

exact_metrics._reading: CE and top-1 are EXACT under the coarse partition by construction, and the measurement confirms it: every .nll metric moves by at most 1.4e-07 and top-1 is bit-identical.

forward_kl_moves._reading: the headline equal-domain mean moves 1.8e-03 relative and the worst-domain identity agrees. `general` moves most (1.0e-02), consistent with its flatter distributions holding less mass in the Top-200.

reverse_kl_move._reading: THE ONE METRIC MATERIALLY CHANGED: -18.7% relative. Reverse KL weights by the CANDIDATE's mass, much of which lies outside the reference's Top-200 and collapses into the single tail bucket. It is a genuinely different quantity under this protocol, and that is exactly why item 7 required it on the SAME reference-defined partition rather than a candidate-defined one -- two partitions in one evaluation would have made this invisible.

depth_reduction._upper_bound: the Top-K figure is an UPPER bound: the observer rebuilt the sketch on every call, where a real Top-K run caches it per item.

depth_reference_state._reading: the reference state is the real saving: 16.91 GiB of cached full-vocabulary logits against 144 MB of sketches over the same 59,763 positions, a factor of 120.

state_evaluation._reading: only 5.7% faster and 2% MORE peak memory at this scale, and that is the honest result: the candidate's full [B,T,V] logits still dominate because the output head's O(V) compute is NOT removed. The saving is in the reference state. No claim of O(K) output-head memory is made and none is supported until a chunked output path exists.

identity.legacy_compatibility: ReductionSemantics.distribution_support is OPTIONAL and omitted from as_dict() under the full-vocabulary contract, so every protocol id computed before the field existed recomputes byte-identically. Asserted both ways in tests/initialization/test_distribution_support.py.
